precepts.text: Abijah told Jeroboam that the Lord gave the kingdom to David and his sons by a covenant of salt; the salt is the preserving of the bond.
precepts.point: Salt is a preservative; it keeps a thing fresh. The covenant of salt goes into the brotherhood: we are supposed to preserve our relationships, keep our alliance fresh, and grow together. Everything given to the Levites for sacrifice carried that symbolism.

note.label: Leviticus 2: The Meat Offering of Fine Flour

precepts.why:
Every oblation of the meat offering had to be seasoned with salt, “the salt of the covenant of thy God”, and “with all thine offerings thou shalt offer salt.” Israel has a covenant of salt with the Lord.

Around the 900s BC there was war between Abijah king of Judah and Jeroboam. Abijah set the battle in array with “four hundred thousand chosen men”, and Jeroboam “with eight hundred thousand chosen men, being mighty men of valour.” The northern kingdom far exceeded the southern in numbers, but the numbers did not matter. Abijah stood up upon mount Zemaraim to defuse the war and said, “Hear me, thou Jeroboam, and all Israel; Ought ye not to know that the Lord God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?”

Salt is a preservative; it keeps a thing fresh. The covenant of salt is the preserving of the bond, and it goes into the brotherhood: we are supposed to preserve our relationships, keep our alliance fresh, and grow together. Everything given to the Levites for sacrifice carried that symbolism. And it is physical too: you offer something up, you whip something up, you better season that thing.

precepts.text: Jeroboam cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and made priests after the manner of the nations, so that any man could consecrate himself to serve gods that are no gods.
precepts.point: This is the setting for a division that ran between the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom. After the split, the northern kingdom fell into idolatry and forsook the Levites, so a prophet of the Most High would want nothing to do with their manner of worship.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

precepts.why:
“Have ye not cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and have made you priests after the manner of the nations of other lands? so that whosoever cometh to consecrate himself with a young bullock and seven rams, the same may be a priest of them that are no gods.”

Jeroboam cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and forsook the Levites. He made priests after the manner of the nations, so that any man could consecrate himself to serve gods that are no gods. That is the division that ran between the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom, and it is why the four hundred prophets Ahab gathered could not be trusted, even though Jehoshaphat said, “I am as thou art, my people as thy people, my horses as thy horses.”

precepts.text: Jeroboam, Solomon's industrious servant, lifts his hand against the king, and the prophet Ahijah tears his garment in twelve pieces and gives him ten tribes.
precepts.point: He names Jeroboam as the servant of Solomon who rose up and rebelled against his lord. To understand that rebellion, the account goes back to 1 Kings 11.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

precepts.why:
Abijah names Jeroboam as “the servant of Solomon the son of David” who “is risen up, and hath rebelled against his lord.” To understand that rebellion, go back to 1 Kings 11: “Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephrathite of Zereda, Solomon’s servant … even he lifted up his hand against the king.”

He was industrious: “the man Jeroboam was a mighty man of valour: and Solomon seeing the young man that he was industrious, he made him ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph.”

Then the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him in the field, took the new garment, “and rent it in twelve pieces: And he said to Jeroboam, Take thee ten pieces: for thus saith the Lord, the God of Israel, Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee.”

Against that, Abijah stands on mount Zemaraim and declares that “the Lord God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt.”

precepts.text: Rehoboam was one and forty years old when he began to reign in Jerusalem.
precepts.point: Young and tenderhearted does not mean a small child. Rehoboam was forty and one years old when he began to reign; he simply knew nothing of war, for the land had rest in Solomon's days.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Rehoboam was one and forty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem.”

So when Abijah says Rehoboam “was young and tenderhearted, and could not withstand them”, young and tenderhearted does not mean a small child. Rehoboam was forty and one years old when he began to reign; he simply knew nothing of war, for the land had rest in Solomon's days. That is how “vain men, the children of Belial” gathered unto Jeroboam and strengthened themselves against him.

precepts.text: The Levites left their suburbs and came to Judah, for Jeroboam cast them off from the priest's office and ordained his own priests for the high places and the devils.
precepts.point: Jeroboam cast out the priests of the Most High, the sons of Aaron and the Levites, and made priests of any man who came to consecrate himself, priests of them that are no gods.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

precepts.why:
“For the Levites left their suburbs and their possession, and came to Judah and Jerusalem: for Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest’s office unto the Lord.”

That is what Abijah throws at Jeroboam: “Have ye not cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and have made you priests after the manner of the nations of other lands?” Jeroboam ordained his own priests for the high places and the devils, and made priests of any man who came to consecrate himself “with a young bullock and seven rams”, so that the same might “be a priest of them that are no gods.”

The great multitude trusted in the “golden calves, which Jeroboam made you for gods”, and in priests after the manner of the nations.

precepts.text: The tribe of Levi is given to Aaron and his sons to wait on the priest's office; the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.
precepts.point: They burn the daily burnt sacrifices morning and evening, set the shewbread in order, and keep the charge of the Most High that Jeroboam forsook.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Bring the tribe of Levi near, and present them before Aaron the priest, that they may minister unto him.” The Levites “shall keep his charge, and the charge of the whole congregation”, and “thou shalt give the Levites unto Aaron and to his sons.”

“And thou shalt appoint Aaron and his sons, and they shall wait on their priest’s office: and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.”

That is the order Judah kept: “the priests, which minister unto the Lord, are the sons of Aaron, and the Levites wait upon their business.” “for we keep the charge of the Lord our God; but ye have forsaken him.” Jeroboam made priests of whoever would consecrate himself, the very strangers the law said must not come nigh.

precepts.text: The one lamb offered in the morning and the other at evening set the pattern of the daily sacrifice.
precepts.point: They burn the daily burnt sacrifices morning and evening, set the shewbread in order, and keep the charge of the Most High that Jeroboam forsook.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

precepts.why:
“The one lamb shalt thou offer in the morning, and the other lamb shalt thou offer at even.”

That is the pattern of the daily sacrifice, and Judah kept it: “they burn unto the Lord every morning and every evening burnt sacrifices and sweet incense.” They set the shewbread in order and lit the golden candlestick every evening. “for we keep the charge of the Lord our God; but ye have forsaken him.”

precepts.text: Thou shalt not forsake the Levite within thy gates, for he has no part nor inheritance with thee.
precepts.point: The great sin the account underlines is Jeroboam casting off the Levites, a law the Most High was very specific about.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

precepts.why:
“And the Levite that is within thy gates; thou shalt not forsake him; for he hath no part nor inheritance with thee.”

The great sin the account underlines is Jeroboam casting off the Levites, and this is a law the Most High was very specific about. Thou shalt not forsake the Levite. Jeroboam did, and Abijah, who stood on the covenant and kept the priests of the Lord, “waxed mighty.”
